options.label: Deterministic low-contention CPU reference
options.effect: CPUExecutionProvider only, FP32, sequential execution, one intra-op and one inter-op thread, spinning disabled, OS-managed affinity, basic graph optimization, CPU arena and memory pattern enabled, profiling and optimized-model output disabled, batch one, one in-flight request, and a two-item queue.
options.tradeoff: Strongest reproducibility and laptop coexistence baseline but intentionally not maximum throughput.

options.label: ONNX Runtime performance defaults
options.effect: Use physical-core thread defaults, spinning enabled, all graph optimizations, CPU arena, and memory pattern.
options.tradeoff: Likely faster but uses more CPU/power and is less stable as a collaborator-laptop reference.

options.label: Hardware-adaptive automatic tuning
options.effect: Choose threads, spinning, arena, and optimization settings from detected capacity.
options.tradeoff: Matches the future dynamic platform goal but requires implementation and generated tuning evidence before it can be trusted.

options.label: Defer runtime configuration
options.tradeoff: Avoids an early choice but prevents a reproducible calibration proposal.

options.label: Bounded three-seed CONTRACT plus INFER matrix
options.effect: Use 64 contract cases; zero, ramp, and three seeded uniform FP32 tensors; three cold starts; five warmups per seed; three repetitions of 30 measured inferences per seed; an eight-request bounded burst; three dependency-loss cases; three safe shutdowns; and a 15-minute total timeout with zero raw retention.
options.tradeoff: Broad deterministic coverage while still bounded for the current laptop; stronger hardware can reuse the same shape at higher later evidence tiers.

options.label: Minimal smoke matrix
options.effect: Use one seed, one cold start, three warmups, ten measured inferences, no burst, and one shutdown.
options.tradeoff: Very fast but weak for queue, recovery, variance, and objective-mode planning.

options.label: Resource-aggressive portable matrix
options.effect: Use ten seeds, ten repetitions, 1,000 measured inferences per seed, and sustained bursts.
options.tradeoff: Higher statistical volume but unsuitable as the first laptop-safe baseline and would require explicit stress/thermal authority.

options.label: Defer exact workload
options.effect: Retain scenario names without counts, seeds, or timeouts.
options.tradeoff: Leaves calibration non-reproducible and blocks the next package.

options.label: Hard safety gates plus calibration then held-out validation
options.effect: Predeclare exact no-fallback, contract, determinism, retention, memory, queue, failure-detection, shutdown, and total-time ceilings now; run a later separately authorized non-promotional calibration; then seal latency, throughput, resource, and recovery thresholds plus held-out seeds before final validation.
options.tradeoff: Avoids invented performance numbers and test-set leakage but requires two separate evidence gates and owner reviews.

options.label: Single-pass fixed conservative thresholds
options.effect: Set latency, throughput, memory, and recovery pass/fail numbers before any calibration and use the first run as final evidence.
options.tradeoff: Faster but thresholds are weakly justified and the first execution becomes both tuning and final evaluation.

options.label: Throughput-first gate
options.effect: Make sustained throughput the primary pass condition and treat latency/resource/recovery as informational.
options.tradeoff: Conflicts with balanced-default and fail-closed evidence policy.

options.label: Structural gates only
options.effect: Validate schemas and deterministic output without performance or resource acceptance.
options.tradeoff: Useful for CONTRACT evidence but insufficient for profile admission or capacity claims.

options.label: Five-revision gated bundle
options.effect: Use R0 planning skeleton, R1 supply-chain-reviewed artifacts, R2 non-promotional generated calibration, R3 held-out validation candidate, and R4 eligible-or-rejected only after all seven resolver inputs and gates pass.
options.tradeoff: Most auditable and portable across laptops, servers, and Kubernetes, but requires explicit authority at each state transition.

options.label: Single mutable bundle
options.effect: Update one manifest in place as artifacts and evidence arrive.
options.tradeoff: Simpler but loses immutable review boundaries and rollback traceability.

options.label: Two revisions only
options.effect: Use candidate and approved revisions, combining acquisition, calibration, and validation evidence.
options.tradeoff: Less overhead but weak separation between research, tuning, final evidence, and promotion.

options.label: Runtime-generated manifest
options.effect: Let the runtime construct compatibility state from the live environment.
options.tradeoff: Dynamic but non-reproducible and incompatible with immutable pre-admission review.
